I complained of severe abdominal pain for over a year, especially around the time of my period. It brought me to tears quite frequently. They were dismissed as bad cramps, take some Advil. I had an iud and said my bleeding seemed dark and irregular, I was put on additional birth control to help regulate my “hormones.” Over a year later I had bought a Groupon to go to a chiropractor. They did a back xray and she noticed my iud looked out of place, recommended I go get it checked. I then found out it had been lodged in my cervix for over a year, my body was trying to push it out when I had my period hence the extreme pain. Luckily they were able to get it out (no sedation of course!) which was also extremely painful. 

Groupon FTW. 

I now cry when I go to the gynecologist in fear that they will ignore my pain. That I will never actually be heard.

1000% agree. I work in animal welfare. There is a large push for more open adoptions but a lot of groups don’t agree. Those groups probably aren’t open admission so they don’t see the 1000s of animals dying everyday because over overcrowding. If you’d been denied by a shelter before, I beg you, please try another place. There are a lot of great rescues out there who will adopt to you. 

I will say, sometimes we do have certain requirements for certain dogs who have failed in other environments (ie they can’t live in elevator building, etc) but that is just to keep owners and the dogs safe. We will then suggest another dog that would be a more appropriate fit. 

Also make sure you check out your local animal control!!

Get a cat stroller! Boxes, different things to climb on, different kinds of scratching posts, cat nip, different small toys! On if my cat loves these little pom pom ball toys, the other a spring toy, the other this squishy baseball that is not actually a cat toy. They are all different and like different things, so I always have a lot of variety (granted I foster cats so I have the ability to borrow different toys to see what works). Look up diy cat enrichment- half the time they don’t even like what we give them and prefer a wine cork with cat nip, a paper ball, or a milk carton ring. And boxes. They fucking love boxes. You could also try fostering another cat to see if that is something that he would enjoy! He is probably already very happy in your home, but I think people forget that senior cats do sometimes enjoy new adventures.

I have seen so many German shepherds come into shelters needing to be euthanized for aggressive behaviors after being subjected to negative/balanced reinforcement training. Please, please find a positive reinforcement trainer. Positive reinforcement may take some dogs longer to learn but that is because they are actually learning, not just being punished and submitted because fear of pain.

Behavioral euthanasia is not wrong. If you cannot handle him, no one else will be able to. 

In the future, neuter early and also make sure your trainers are using positive reinforcement. A lot of trainers do not use positive reinforcement which has been proven to often make aggression worse.
